title: Copilot Credits: the shared meter for usage-based AI billing
summary: The billing, licensing and actionable spending controls support publication. The claim that user reporting is exclusive to standard-harness agents goes beyond Microsoft's wording and should be narrowed; minor corrections concern a missing citation and a checklist setting absent from the controls table.

claims.claim: Identity-based spending policies and monthly limits are configured in Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > Add spending policy.
claims.quote: In the Microsoft 365 admin center, go to **Copilot > Cost Management**. ... Select the **Configuration** tab and then select **+ Add spending policy**.

claims.claim: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies creates a policy using a concrete allUsersSpendingPolicy type and displayName, periodLimit, perUserLimit and serviceSettings.
claims.quote: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies ... Required properties are `displayName`, `periodLimit`, `perUserLimit`, and `serviceSettings`.

claims.claim: Resource-based policies are created in Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > Add spending policy > Resources.
claims.quote: go to **Copilot > Cost Management**. ... Select **Configuration**, and then select **Add spending policy**. ... Enter a name for the policy, then select **Resources** as its scope.

claims.claim: Microsoft documents no API for creating resource-based spending policies at the time of writing in November 2026.
claims.quote: Searched: 'copilot costManagement resource-based spendingPolicies API create resource policy'; 'spendingPolicy resource graph'. Opened Create spendingPolicy and Cost Management API overview: only all-users and selected-groups audiences are documented.

claims.claim: A spending policy's billing method can be changed through Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration > spending policy.
claims.quote: The **Configuration** tab within the Cost management page is displayed. ... You can update the billing method for an existing spending policy. Open the spending policy that you want to modify and update its billing method.

claims.claim: POST to the beta spendingPolicies endpoint can select billingMethods prepaidCredits during policy creation, rather than updating an existing policy.
claims.quote: POST https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies ... You can optionally supply `billingMethods`. ... "billingMethods": "prepaidCredits"

claims.claim: Policy and per-user alerts are available in the Add spending policy workflow under Copilot > Cost Management > Configuration.
claims.quote: Select the **Configuration** tab and then select **+ Add spending policy**. ... Configure policy-level alerts: ... If the policy has a monthly per-user limit, configure user-level threshold notifications:

claims.claim: PATCH https://graph.microsoft.com/beta/copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id}/emailThresholdSettings accepts isEnabled and thresholds with percentageCostManagementAlertThreshold and value.
claims.quote: PATCH /copilot/costManagement/spendingPolicies/{id}/emailThresholdSettings ... "isEnabled": true, ... { "@odata.type": "#microsoft.graph.percentageCostManagementAlertThreshold", "value": 80 }

claims.claim: Environment allocation is managed in Power Platform admin center > Licensing > Products > Copilot Studio > Summary > Manage Capacity > environment.
claims.quote: select **Licensing**. ... under **Products**, select **Copilot Studio**. ... Select the **Summary** tab. ... Select **Manage Capacity** from the **Prepaid capacity** card. ... In the allocation panel, select an environment

claims.claim: Consumption by policy, user, group, agent and service is available in Microsoft 365 admin center > Copilot > Cost management > Consumption.

claims.fix: Add https://learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-365/copilot/extensibility/api/admin-settings/cost-management/resources/allusersspendingpolicy to sources; it explicitly documents the all-users scope.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risks and limits: Switching environments
claims.claim: A resource-based spending policy replaces Power Platform capacity allocations for environments it covers.
claims.quote: Existing Power Platform capacity allocations and linked billing plans don't apply while spending for that environment is managed by a resource-based spending policy in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.where: controls[1].note; Risks and limits: Switching environments
claims.claim: The linked Power Platform billing plan also stops applying while the environment is covered by the Microsoft 365 resource-based policy.
claims.quote: Existing Power Platform capacity allocations and linked billing plans don't apply while spending for that environment is managed by a resource-based spending policy in the Microsoft 365 admin center.

claims.claim: Global administrator and Billing administrator can add and change billing methods and set them in policies.
claims.quote: Global administrator and Billing administrator roles can add, select, and change billing methods, and set billing methods in policies.

claims.claim: The Graph alert configuration is notify-only.
claims.quote: Thresholds notify recipients but don't increase limits or authorize consumption.

claims.claim: The emailThresholdSettings operation configures policy-level alerts, not per-user threshold notifications.
claims.quote: Notify-only alert configuration for a spending policy, addressed as the policy's `emailThresholdSettings`. Each policy has at most one, retrieved from its own URL beneath the policy.

claims.claim: Updating emailThresholdSettings requires If-Match with the parent policy's ETag.
claims.quote: `If-Match` | The ETag of the parent spending policy. Required.

claims.claim: Alert recipients are managed separately from the PATCH request body.
claims.quote: Recipients can't be sent inline. Manage them through the recipient `$ref` endpoints

claims.claim: At least one recipient must be linked before enabling alerts.
claims.quote: Enabling alerting while no recipient is linked is refused with a `400 alertRecipientsRequired` response.

claims.claim: Programmatic allocation requires Power Platform Administrator, Global Administrator or an equivalent licensing-and-capacity role.
claims.quote: Sign in as a user with the **Power Platform Administrator** or **Global Administrator** role, or an equivalent role that can manage licensing and capacity.

claims.claim: Disabling TenantPool corresponds to clearing Draw from the available capacity in my tenant and caps prepaid consumption at the environment allocation.
claims.quote: The **Draw from the available capacity in my tenant** option in the admin center maps to the `TenantPool` enforcement rule ... when it's disabled, the environment is capped at its allocation.

claims.claim: Enabling TenantPool lets the environment draw from unallocated tenant capacity after exhausting its allocation.
claims.quote: when it's enabled, the environment continues to draw from unallocated tenant capacity after its own allocation is exhausted

claims.claim: Turning off tenant-pool draw does not disable consumption through a linked pay-as-you-go plan.
claims.quote: This setting doesn't prevent consumption through a pay-as-you-go billing plan linked to the environment.

claims.claim: A published environment-group rule for tenant-capacity draw blocks per-environment changes in both the admin center and API.
claims.quote: you can't override the setting for an individual environment. Updates through the Power Platform admin center, Power Platform API, or administration SDKs are rejected with the `TenantPoolLockedByPolicy` error.
